rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports four figures who spoke as infants: this child, Joseph’s witness, the companion of Jurayj, and Jesus son of Mary.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وتكلم أربعة وهم صغار هذا وشاهد يوسف وصاحب جريح وعيسى بن مريم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet saw preachers whose lips were cut by fiery shears and regrew; Gabriel identified them as preachers who say what they do not practice.
rows.anchor: عن أنس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barzakh representations picture deeds through their outcomes and prepared punishments and recur frequently in Isra reports.
rows.anchor: وهذا النوع من التمثلات البرزخية التي تصور الأعمال بنتائجها والعذابات المعدة لها كثيرة الورود في أخبار الإسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Isra reports reach tawātur, transmitted by many Companions and many Shiʿi narrators from the Imams.
rows.anchor: وهي كثيرة بالغة حد التواتر رواها جم غفير من الصحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars whose views count agree the Isra occurred in Mecca before the Hijra; Quraysh’s denial the next morning and the Prophet’s descriptions support this.
rows.anchor: وقد اتفقت أقوال من يعتني بقوله من علماء الإسلام على أن الإسراء كان بمكة قبل الهجرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One reported chronology places the Isra in the second year of the prophetic mission.
rows.anchor: فقيل في السنة الثانية من البعثة كما عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report in al-Kharāʾij places it in the third year of the mission.
rows.anchor: وقيل في السنة الثالثة منها كما في الخرائج عن علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports place it in the fifth or sixth year.
rows.anchor: وقيل في السنة الخامسة أو السادسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report dates it ten years and three months after the mission began.
rows.anchor: وقيل بعد البعثة بعشر سنين وثلاثة أشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report dates it to the twelfth year of the mission.
rows.anchor: وقيل في السنة الثانية عشرة منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some date it one year and five months before the Hijra.
rows.anchor: وقيل قبل الهجرة بسنة وخمسة أشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some date it one year and three months before the Hijra.
rows.anchor: وقيل قبلها بسنة وثلاثة أشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some date it six months before the Hijra.
rows.anchor: وقيل قبلها بستة أشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī sees no need to investigate the date because no dependable evidence establishes it.
rows.anchor: ولا يهمنا الغور في البحث عن ذلك ولا عن الشهر واليوم الذي وقع فيه الإسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahl al-Bayt reports explicitly indicate two Isra journeys, also suggested by Qurʾān 53:13.
rows.anchor: من الروايات المأثورة عن أئمة أهل البيت عليه السلام ما يصرح بوقوع الإسراء مرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If there were two Isra journeys, differing reports about extraordinary sights can describe the first, the second, or both.
rows.anchor: ما وصفه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في بعض الروايات من عجيب ما شاهده راجعا إلى ما شاهده في الإسراء الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports differ on the starting place: the ravine of Abū Ṭālib or Umm Hāniʾ’s house; some interpret the Sacred Mosque as the whole sanctuary to include Mecca.
rows.anchor: فقيل أسري به من شعب أبي طالب وقيل أسري به من بيت أم هاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others take the verse’s apparent wording literally and say the journey began inside the Sacred Mosque; he sees no need for figurative interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقيل أسري به من نفس المسجد الحرام لظهور الآية الكريمة فيه ولا دليل على التأويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two journeys could reconcile the locations: one from the Sacred Mosque and another from Umm Hāniʾ’s house.
rows.anchor: ومن الجائز بالنظر إلى ما نبهنا به من كون الإسراء مرتين أن يكون أحد الإسراءين من المسجد الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ravine account conflicts with reports of Abū Ṭālib searching and threatening Quraysh all night, and with the family’s hardship while confined there.
rows.anchor: ثم نزوله من السماء ومجيئه إليهم وإخباره قريشا بما رأى كل ذلك لا يلائم ما كان هو صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وبنو هاشم جميعا عليه من الشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority say the Prophet traveled bodily and spiritually from the Sacred Mosque to Jerusalem and then ascended to heaven.
rows.anchor: فقيل كان إسراؤه عليه السلام بروحه وجسده من المسجد الحرام إلى بيت المقدس ثم منه إلى السماوات وعليه الأكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another group says he went bodily and spiritually from Mecca to Jerusalem, then ascended from Jerusalem in spirit alone.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان بروحه وجسده من مكة إلى بيت المقدس ثم بروحه من بيت المقدس إلى السماوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view, attributed to some, makes the journey a true dream experienced by the Prophet’s spirit alone.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان بروحه عليه السلام وهو رؤيا صادقة أراها الله نبيه

rows.speaker: الخوارج
rows.claim: The account quoted from al-Manāqib says the Khārijites deny the Ascension.
rows.anchor: فالخوارج ينكرونه

rows.speaker: الجهمية
rows.claim: The Jahmiyya hold that only the spirit ascended, as a dream.
rows.anchor: وقالت الجهميه عرج بروحه دون جسمه على طريق الرؤيا

rows.speaker: الإمامية والزيدية والمعتزلة
rows.claim: Imamis, Zaydis, and Muʿtazilites affirm a bodily and spiritual journey to Jerusalem, citing this verse.
rows.anchor: وقالت الإمامية والزيدية والمعتزلة بل عرج بروحه وبجسمه إلى البيت المقدس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود وجابر وحذيفة وأنس وعائشة وأم هاني
rows.claim: Other reports attributed to these Companions say the Prophet ascended bodily and spiritually to the heavens.
rows.anchor: روي ذلك عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود وجابر وحذيفة وأنس وعائشة وأم هاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basic Isra cannot be denied: the Qurʾān states it and reports from the Prophet and Ahl al-Bayt Imams are mutawātir.
rows.anchor: إن أصل الإسراء مما لا سبيل إلى إنكاره فقد نص عليه القرآن وتواترت عليه الأخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse and corroborating reports establish travel bodily and spiritually from the Sacred Mosque to Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: ظهورا لا يقبل الدفع أنه أسري به من المسجد الحرام إلى المسجد الأقصى بروحه وجسده جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ascension to heaven is established by Sūrat al-Najm and numerous explicit reports, so its occurrence cannot be denied.
rows.anchor: وصريح الروايات على كثرتها البالغة وقوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A spirit-only account is possible only as a real spiritual journey, not a dream: a dream explains neither the divine display of power nor Quraysh’s denial and the travel reports.
rows.anchor: ولو كان كذلك لم يكن لما يدل عليه الآيات بسياقها من إظهار المقدرة والكرامة معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Materialist interpreters treat unseen beings as subtle matter because they restrict real existence to matter besides God.
rows.anchor: الوجود المادي وقصر الوجود غير المادي فيه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They reduce spiritual stations and deeds’ outcomes to similes, leading to sophistry, distorted perception, and arbitrary links between acts and outcomes.
rows.anchor: حملوا أيضا ما ورد من التمثيلات في مقامات الصالحين ومعارج القرب وبواطن صور المعاصي ونتائج الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deny bodily ascent force it into a dream and reinterpret verses and reports against their fit.
rows.anchor: اضطروا إلى القول بكونه في المنام وهو عندهم خاصة مادية للروح المادي

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Majmaʿ al-Bayān says the destination was Jerusalem as the Qurʾān states; sleep is a false account because it would contain no miracle or proof.
rows.anchor: فإن الإسراء إلى بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Its first category is certainly authentic because of tawātur and established knowledge.
rows.anchor: أحدها ما يقطع على صحتها لتواتر الأخبار به وإحاطة العلم بصحته

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Its second category contains rationally possible reports; accept them and affirm the event occurred while awake.
rows.anchor: وثانيها ما ورد في ذلك مما يجوزه العقول ولا يأباه الأصول فنحن نجوزه

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Its third category appears to conflict with principles but can be interpreted rationally, so should be interpreted accordingly.
rows.anchor: وثالثها ما يكون ظاهره مخالفا لبعض الأصول إلا أنه يمكن تأويلها على وجه يوافق المعقول

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Its fourth category has an invalid apparent sense and only a strained interpretation, so should be rejected.
rows.anchor: ورابعها ما لا يصح ظاهره ولا يمكن تأويله إلا على التعسف البعيد

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Reports of the heavenly tour and seeing prophets, the Throne, the Lote Tree, Paradise, and Hell belong in its rationally possible second category.
rows.anchor: وأما الثاني فمنه ما روي أنه طاف في السماوات ورأى الأنبياء والعرش

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: It interprets people seen enjoying Paradise or punished in Hell as their qualities or names, in the interpretable third category.
rows.anchor: وأما الثالث فنحو ما روي أنه رأى قوما في الجنة يتنعمون فيها وقوما في النار يعذبون فيها

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: It rejects reports that God spoke openly to the Prophet, was seen, or sat on a throne because their apparent meaning anthropomorphizes God.
rows.anchor: ونحو ذلك مما يوجب ظاهره التشبيه

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: It rejects the report of the Prophet’s abdomen being opened and washed, reasoning that water cannot purify belief.
rows.anchor: وكيف يطهر القلب وما فيه من الاعتقاد بالماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī accepts the four-part framework but says most examples assigned to its categories need reconsideration.
rows.anchor: وما ذكره من التقسيم في محله غير أن غالب ما أورده من الأمثلة للأقسام منظور فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing prophets and touring the heavens, as well as abdomen washing, can be barzakh or spiritual representations rather than objectionable physical events.
rows.anchor: فما ذكره من الطواف ورؤية الأنبياء ونحو ذلك تمثلات برزخية أو روحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accounts variously describe ascent by Buraq, Gabriel’s wing, or a ladder on Jerusalem’s rock; these variations indicate spiritual representation.
rows.anchor: صعوده صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إلى السماء بالبراق وفي آخر على جناح جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Representational forms occur in the outward language of Qurʾān and Sunna and cannot be denied.
rows.anchor: ووقوع هذه التمثيلات في ظواهر الكتاب والسنة مما لا سبيل إلى إنكاره البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening seven verses portray God’s practice: guide human communities to servitude and monotheism, enable choice, and provide means for obedience and disobedience; good brings happiness in both lives, evil punishment.
rows.anchor: أن السنة الإلهية في الأمم الإنسانية جرت على هدايتهم إلى طريق العبودية وسبيل التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel exemplifies this pattern: revelation and warning, punishment through enemy domination, renewed blessing after obedience, then a second punishment after renewed transgression, with mercy hoped for if they return.
rows.anchor: أنزل الله على نبيهم الكتاب وجعله لهم هدى يهتدون به وقضى إليهم فيه أنهم سيعلون ويطغون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven verses prepare for the same divine practice among this Muslim community and interrupt the transition from verse 1 to verse 9.
rows.anchor: الآيات السبع كالتوطئة لما سيذكر بعدها من جريان هذه السنة العامة في هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kitāb often denotes the full set of written ordinances for belief and practice; saying Book rather than Torah may emphasize comprehensive obligations.
rows.anchor: الكتاب كثيرا ما يطلق في كلامه تعالى على مجموع الشرائع المكتوبة على الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Book guidance explains its gift: it sets out divine laws which, if followed, lead Israel to truth and happiness in both lives.
rows.anchor: وكونه هدى أي هاديا لهم هو بيانه لهم شرائع ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle an explains the Book’s essential teaching: do not associate anything with God or take another as trustee; its pronoun apparently addresses Israel, though it may address Moses and Israel together.
rows.anchor: ان فيه للتفسير ومدخولها محصل ما يشتمل عليه الكتاب الذي جعل هدى لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from plural divine speech to singular underscores monotheism; “do not take trustees besides Us” would not fit, so plural speech resumes afterward.
rows.anchor: ولذلك عدل فيها إلى سياق التكلم وحده ثم لما ارتفعت الحاجة رجع الكلام إلى سياقه السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A trustee manages a principal’s essential affairs and needs; since God alone does so, treating another as lord amounts to taking a trustee besides Him and associating partners.
rows.anchor: أن الوكيل هو الذي يكفل إصلاح الشؤون الضرورية لموكله ويقدم على رفع حوائجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhurriyya can denote children as young and dependent on parents; here it is an accusative of specification, adding emphasis and functioning causally.
rows.anchor: تطلق الذرية على الأولاد بعناية كونهم صغارا ملحقين بآبائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The specification works like “Ahl al-Bayt” in 33:33: the group is singled out as the reason for the preceding divine action.
rows.anchor: يفيد الاختصاص عناية خاصة من المتكلم به في حكمه فهو بمنزلة التعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel receives the Book as descendants of Noah’s passengers, fulfilling the promise of peace, blessing, and provision to Noah’s people after the flood.
rows.anchor: في إنزاله الكتاب لموسى وجعله هدى لبني إسرائيل إنجاز للوعد الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s gratitude explains enduring guidance: he established monotheistic guidance among humankind, and gratitude entails sincere servitude, for which God preserved and rewarded his way.
rows.anchor: هذه السنة أعني سنة الهداية والإرشاد وطريقة الدعوة إلى التوحيد هي بعينها السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewarded Noah’s gratitude by preserving his call among those carried with him, including through the Book given to Moses for Israel.
rows.anchor: أنا أبقينا دعوته وأجرينا سنته وطريقته في ذرية من حملناهم معه في السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two textual hints support descendants through sons and daughters; if only sons were meant, “Noah’s descendants” would be the more apt wording.
rows.anchor: أن الناس ذرية نوح عليه السلام من جهة الابن والبنت معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He dismisses as implausible parses making dhurriyya a vocative, an object of “take” and trustee, or a substitute for Moses.
rows.anchor: وهي وجوه ظاهرة السخافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also finds implausible the reading that “he” refers to Moses rather than Noah, whether explaining the Book’s gift or making Moses guidance for Israel.
rows.anchor: عائد إلى موسى دون نوح والجملة تعليل لإيتائه الكتاب

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines divine verbal decree as decisive command or disclosure: God informed Israel with finality in revelation, as in 15:66.
rows.anchor: فهذا قضاء بالاعلام والفصل في الحكم أي أعلمناهم وأوحينا إليهم وحيا جزما

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib distinguishes divine creative decree from human verbal judgment and human acts such as completing rites.
rows.anchor: والله يقضى بالحق والذين يدعون من دونه لا يقضون بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Exalting themselves” means tyrannical oppression and transgression, clarified by pairing it with corruption and by Pharaoh in 28:4.
rows.anchor: والعلو هو الارتفاع وهو في الآية كناية عن الطغيان بالظلم والتعدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two corruptions and acts of great arrogance concern Israel’s repeated oppression in Palestine and its surroundings.
rows.anchor: ستفسدون في الأرض وهي أرض فلسطين وما يتبعها مرتين مرة بعد مرة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says buʾs and baʾs denote hardship, especially poverty and war for the former and punishment or destruction for the latter.
rows.anchor: إلا أن البؤس في الفقر والحرب أكثر والبأس والبأساء في النكاية

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayd glosses jawasū as entering, mixing through, and treading a place; another gloss is exhaustive searching.
rows.anchor: كل موضع خالطته ووطأته فقد حسته وجسته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first promise means punishment for the first corruption; its “coming” is a metonym for the time of fulfillment, and the context implies two promised punishments.
rows.anchor: والمراد بوعد أولاهما ما وعدهم الله من النكال والنقمة على إفسادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s sending severe warriors is humiliation and retaliation for Israel’s corruption, not injustice, since Israel wronged themselves.
rows.anchor: لأنه كان على سبيل المجازاة على إفسادهم في الأرض وعلوهم وبغيهم بغير الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording does not prove God ordered believers to fight Israel; even unbelievers can be God’s servants when their defeat of Israel serves retribution.
rows.anchor: أمرنا قوما مؤمنين بقتالكم وجهادكم لاقتضاء ظاهر قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative that unbelievers were recruited by a prophet to fight Israel also lacks support in the wording.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكونوا كفارا فتألفهم نبي من الأنبياء لحرب هؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first punishment is certain: warriors entered in conquest, penetrated homes, humiliated Israel, and ended its independence.
rows.anchor: فدخلوا بالقهر والغلبة أرضكم وتوسطوا في دياركم فأذلوكم

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ glosses al-kurra as return or restored power, and al-nafīr as the number of men.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع الكرة معناه الرجعة والدولة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj allows al-nafīr as a plural of nafar; related forms mean a supporting clan who mobilize with a person.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون جمع نفر كما قيل العبيد والضئين والمعيز والكليب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel regains power over the first enemies gradually over substantial time, strengthened by wealth, children, and a larger force.
rows.anchor: وأن هذه الدولة سترجع إليهم تدريجا في برهة معتد بها من الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restored victory followed Israel’s return to good conduct after suffering for wrongdoing; the second punishment followed renewed wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: إنما كانت لرجوعهم إلى الإحسان بعد ما ذاقوا وبال إساءتهم قبل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām marks restriction: each deed’s consequence belongs to its agent; the verse concerns ownership of consequences, not merely benefit versus harm.
rows.anchor: للاختصاص أي ان كلا من إحسانكم وإساءتكم يختص بأنفسكم دون أن يلحق غيركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects readings that make the lām mean “against,” “toward,” or entitlement, since the context is not merely that good helps and evil harms its agent.
rows.anchor: وقول آخرين إنها للاستحقاق كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afterlife effects never transfer; worldly effects reach others only if God wills favor, adversity, or trial, while the agent always bears a consequence.
rows.anchor: أما آثار الأعمال الأخروية فإنها لا تتعدى صاحبها البتة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī reportedly said a person neither did good to nor harmed anyone else, then recited this verse.
rows.anchor: ما أحسنتم إلى أحد ولا أسأت إليه وتلا الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabarr means destruction; the purpose clause describes grief, humiliation, captivity, and visible subjection.
rows.anchor: بعثناهم ليسوؤا وجوهكم بظهور الحزن والكآبة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mosque is Jerusalem’s al-Aqsa, not the Holy Land metaphorically; the verse implies the first invaders entered it by force to desecrate it and suggests they returned.
rows.anchor: المراد بالمسجد هو المسجد الأقصى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What they conquered” is the preferred meaning of mā; the alternative is “the duration of their dominance,” but the former better fits the context.
rows.anchor: والمعنى الأول أقرب إلى الفهم وأوفق بالسياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second punishment is harsher, nearly annihilating Israel, as destruction of everything they dominated indicates.
rows.anchor: أن الثاني كان أشد على بني إسرائيل وأمر وقد كادوا أن يفنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaṣīr derives from confinement; Gehenna is a prison for unbelievers from which they cannot escape.
rows.anchor: الحصير من الحصر وهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hope of mercy follows the second punishment and assumes Israel repents and returns to obedience and good conduct.
rows.anchor: أي بعد البعث الثاني على ما يفيده السياق وهو ترج للرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Israel returns again to corruption and arrogance after repentance, God will return to punishment and humiliation.
rows.anchor: أي وإن تعودوا إلى الإفساد والعلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to “your Lord” signals that mercy is the default of God’s lordship when people follow their created nature and fitra; plural speech resumes afterward.
rows.anchor: الإشارة إلى أن الأصل الذي يقتضيه ربوبيته تعالى أن يرحم عباده

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar says Noah was called grateful because morning and evening he credited God alone for every religious or worldly blessing and well-being, praising and thanking Him until He was pleased.
rows.anchor: إن نوحا إنما سمي عبدا شكورا لأنه كان يقول إذا أمسى وأصبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same meaning, with slight variation, is transmitted in several routes in al-Kāfī and the tafsirs of al-Qummī and al-ʿAyyāshī.
rows.anchor: وروي هذا المعنى بتفاوت يسير بعدة طرق في الكافي وتفسيري القمي والعياشي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abū Fāṭima reports that the Prophet said Noah praised God whenever he picked up anything, small or large, so God called him grateful.
rows.anchor: عن أبي فاطمة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This report fits gratitude as sincere servitude: Noah’s prayer reflected realizing its truth, inseparable from sincerity in worship.
rows.anchor: والروايات لا تنافي ما تقدم من تفسير الشكر بالإخلاص

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh applies the two corruptions to killing ʿAlī and wounding al-Ḥasan, the great arrogance to killing al-Ḥusayn, and the first promise to al-Ḥusayn’s victory; avengers will act before the Qāʾim for wrongs against Muḥammad’s family.
rows.anchor: عن صالح بن سهل عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قول الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports apply Muslim history to Israel’s pattern, echoing the mutawātir Prophetic prediction that this community would imitate Israel step by step; they are not interpretations of the verses, as differing applications show.
rows.anchor: وليست الروايات واردة في تفسير الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Historical narratives about Israel’s two catastrophes conflict too greatly to rely on, so he omits them.
rows.anchor: فقد اختلفت الروايات فيها اختلافا عجيبا يسلب عنها التعويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many events could fit, but the generally accepted first destruction is by Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar about six centuries BCE, after Israel rebelled.
rows.anchor: أن إحدى هاتين النكايتين اللتين تشير إليهما الآيات هي ما جرى عليهم بيد بخت نصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nebuchadnezzar devastated the land and Temple, burned scripture, killed most people, and deported a small remnant to Babylon; Cyrus later permitted their return and rebuilding.
rows.anchor: فخرب البلاد وهدم المسجد الأقصى وأحرق التوراة وكتب الأنبياء وأباد النفوس بالقتل العام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Cyrus enabled Ezra to rewrite the Torah in the mid-fifth century BCE; Jewish history says the first destruction lasted seventy years.
rows.anchor: وأجاز لعزراء أحد كهنتهم أن يكتب لهم التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jewish history identifies the second destruction with Roman Caesar Vespasian sending his minister Titus to ruin the Temple and humiliate Israel.
rows.anchor: والمبعوث ثانيا هو قيصر الروم إسبيانوس سير إليهم وزيره طوطوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Babylonian and Roman catastrophes plausibly fit because other events did not erase Israel’s community and sovereignty; they later reassembled, then Rome ended their power.
rows.anchor: لكن نازلة بخت نصر ذهب بجميعهم وسؤددهم إلى زمن كورش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses imply the same people attacked twice and that Israel’s restored victory was over its first attackers, while the later pronoun may refer back to them.
rows.anchor: فيها إشعارا بأن المبعوث إلى بني إسرائيل في المرة الأولى والثانية قوم بأعيانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are implications, not clear proof: Israel could have prevailed over different enemies, and the later pronoun can refer to people implied by context rather than the first invaders.
rows.anchor: لكنه إشعار من غير دلالة ظاهرة لجواز أن يكون المراد كرة من غير بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier passage explains divine guidance, reward, and punishment, using Moses’ Torah and Israel as an example; the new passage applies the same pattern to this community.
rows.anchor: وكان ذكر نزول التوراة وما جرى بعد ذلك على بني إسرائيل كالمثال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior discussion yields the duty to avoid association and adhere to monotheism, stated as the prohibition on taking another god beside God.
rows.anchor: وقد استنتج من الآيات لزوم التجنب عن الشرك ووجوب التزام طريق التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān guides to the most upright religion, as in 6:161; qiyām names a balanced, capable posture and becomes a metaphor for managing and caring for affairs well.
rows.anchor: والأقوم أفعل تفضيل والأصل في الباب القيام ضد القعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ḥanīf religion is upright because it governs human welfare in both lives and accords with human fitra and the nature God created in people.
rows.anchor: وليس إلا لكونه موافقا لما تقتضيه الفطرة الإنسانية والخلقه التي سواه الله سبحانه عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Compared with human-made ways, Islam is more upright because other systems may help some areas while harming or neglecting others, whereas it governs all that matters in both lives.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذلك الإسلام يقوم على حياتهم وبجميع ما يهمهم في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Compared with earlier divine laws, the Qurʾānic religion is more complete, giving the furthest knowledge humans can bear and comprehensive individual and social legislation, overseeing prior scripture.
rows.anchor: هذه الملة الحنيفية أكمل من الملل السابقة التي تتضمنها كتب الأنبياء السابقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Good works” abbreviates “they perform good works”; the promised reward is a right God established for believing doers, creating no obligation on Him from outside.
rows.anchor: الصالحات صفة محذوف موصوفها اختصارا والتقدير وعملوا الأعمال الصالحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers without good works have no fixed promised wage; their case remains subject to repentance or intercession, though faith establishes steadfastness and a firm footing.
rows.anchor: وأما من آمن ولم يعمل الصالحات فليس ممن له على الله أجر منجز وحق ثابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿtād means preparing or storing something ahead of need; punishment coordinates with the prior promise and is glad news to believers because God punishes their religious opponents.
rows.anchor: الإعتاد الإعداد والتهيئة من العتاد بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelief in the afterlife is singled out because the upright religion has no purpose without resurrection, even if someone accepts monotheism; forgetting Judgment is a root of deviation.
rows.anchor: ولا موقع للدين ولا فائدة له مع إنكار المعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duʿāʾ means any request, verbal or enacted through pursuit, since God alone truly gives and withholds; seeking is a request of God whether one realizes it or not.
rows.anchor: المراد بالدعاء على ما يستفاد من السياق مطلق الطلب سواء كان بلفظ الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human haste means pursuing desire without pausing to consider benefit or harm, so one may rush toward something harmful or beneficial.
rows.anchor: لا يأخذ بالأناة إذا أراد شيئا حتى يتروى ويتفكر في جهات صلاحه وفساده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 11–12 rebuke humans for neglecting guidance and indiscriminately pursuing good and evil, truth and falsehood; God’s enabling an act does not make every desire or sin permissible.
rows.anchor: والآية وما يتلوها من الآيات في سياق التوبيخ واللوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day illustrate moral distinction: both exist by God’s permission, yet night is effaced for stillness and day made visible for activity; leave evil and pursue good.
rows.anchor: آية الليل ممحوة تسكن فيها الحركات وتهدأ فيها العيون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person’s deeds are his own attached bird, indicating happiness or misery; the deed remains his and cannot be assigned to someone else.
rows.anchor: فإن عمل الإنسان هو طائره الذي يدله على سعادته وشقائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context admonishes humanity’s haste, which keeps people from valuing guidance and leads them to seek misery as impulsively as happiness.
rows.anchor: فهو سبحانه يلوم الإنسان أنه لما به من قريحة الاستعجال لا يقدر نعمة الهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The human” means humankind generally, not only disbelievers; duʿāʾ is unrestricted seeking, and good and evil mean true felicity or misery rather than any benefit or harm.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالإنسان هو الجنس دون أفراد معينة منه كالكفار والمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haste is wanting a desire to become real immediately, not persistence in asking for punishment; other exegetes’ tangled readings are omitted as unhelpful.
rows.anchor: وبالعجلة حب الإنسان أن يسرع ما يهواه إلى التحقق

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr explains “illuminating” as enabling people to see, like idioms attributing sleeping to night or concealment to a secret.
rows.anchor: أراد يبصر بها كما يقال ليل نائم وسر كاتم

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says Arabs use “the day became bright” for the day’s illumination.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي العرب تقول أبصر النهار إذا أضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day are alternating light and darkness as the sun appears and sets; like all created things, they intrinsically signify God’s sole lordship.
rows.anchor: وهما كسائر ما في الكون من أعيان الأشياء وأحوالها آيتان لله سبحانه تدلان بذاتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Making them signs” means creating them as signs; the night itself is effaced by becoming dark and hidden from sight.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بجعلهما آيتين هو خلقهما كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night sign is not the moon with its spots erased, nor the day sign the spotless sun: the verse speaks of night and day themselves, and the purposes concern their darkness and light.
rows.anchor: فإن الكلام في الآيتين لا آيتي الآيتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also rejects taking night as darkness and erasure as its removal by daylight, with the reverse for day, because this erases the contrast between the signs.
rows.anchor: ونظيره في السقوط قول بعضهم إن المراد بآية الليل ظلمته وبآية النهار ضوءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God’s bounty means seeking provision and follows directly from making daytime luminous.
rows.anchor: أي جعلناها مضيئة لتطلبوا فيه رزقا من ربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Supplying an omitted purpose, “so you may rest at night,” is rejected because it makes effects apply to both signs rather than the illuminated day alone.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن التقدير ينافي كون الكلام مسوقا لبيان ترتب الآثار على إحدى الآيتين دون الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People count years by treating a number of days as a unit and use this to calculate times and deadlines; context ties this purpose to visible daytime.
rows.anchor: لتعلموا بمحو الليل وإبصار النهار عدد السنين بجعل عدد من الأيام واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though both night and day help calculation, people sense light first, then infer darkness as its privation; awareness moves from existence to absence.
rows.anchor: إنا إنما نتنبه للآعدام والفقدانات من ناحية الوجودات لا بالعكس

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī proposes that erasing the night sign means the moon’s waxing and waning, whose changing light affects seas, deserts, and human temperaments.
rows.anchor: ما يعرض القمر من اختلاف النور من المحاق إلى المحاق بالزيادة والنقيصة

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī explains that sunlight distinguishes day from night while the moon’s phases mark months and years, enabling provision-seeking and time reckoning.
rows.anchor: فإن الشمس هي التي تميز النهار من الليل والقمر باختلاف تشكلاته يرسم الشهور القمرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects this reading because the admonitory context assigns purposes to distinct signs and answers an excuse for seeking evil as well as good.
rows.anchor: فقد عرفت أن الآيات في سياق التوبيخ واللوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People rush toward evil relying on natural freedom and divine enablement, as in the polytheists’ excuse that God could have prevented their worship; ability does not make evil lawful.
rows.anchor: لو شاء الله ما عبدنا من دونه من شيء نحن ولا آبائنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day are both signs, yet God assigns stillness to night and useful activity to day; good and evil occurring by permission does not make them equally permissible.
rows.anchor: كذلك اشتراك أعمال الخير والشر في أنها جميعا تتحقق بإذن الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that the verse aims to prove monotheism is mistaken: signs’ ability to prove unity does not make that the point in every context.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن دلالتهما على التوحيد لا توجب أن يكون الغرض إفادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing statement that everything is detailed means creation distinguishes things rather than leaving them vague or undifferentiated.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى تمييز الأشياء وأن الخلقة لا تتضمن إبهامها ولا إجمالها

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ says a person’s bird is his deed, likened to birds used for omens: a sanīḥ passes from left to right auspiciously, while a bāriḥ passes right to left ominously.
rows.anchor: الطائر هنا عمل الإنسان شبه بالطائر الذي يسنح ويتبرك به

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abū Zayd says Arabs call anything that passes by, bird or gazelle, a ṭāʾir in this omen practice.
rows.anchor: كل ما يجري من طائر أو ظبي أو غيره فهو عندهم طائر

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf says travelers would make birds fly: passage from left to right was a good omen, from right to left a bad omen, hence taṭayyur.
rows.anchor: فإذا سافروا ومر بهم طير زجروه فإن مر بهم سانحا بأن مر من جهة اليسار إلى اليمين تيمنوا
